extracted.intended_audience: Investigators/applicants preparing NIH grant applications involving live vertebrate animals (and grant reviewers/NIH staff supporting review)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklist for completing the Vertebrate Animals Section (VAS) of NIH grant and contract applications, including what must be described, justified, and reviewed when proposed work involves live vertebrate animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance site identification and per-site description
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant institution is not the site where animal work will be performed or if the work will be performed at several sites, these performance sites (institutions) must be identified. The proposed work involving live vertebrate animals should be described for every performance site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist: If applicant’s institution is not where animal work will be performed, are all collaborative performance sites identified? If more than one performance site is planned, are descriptions of animal use addressing the required criteria provided for each site? (Reviewer/admin will check that descriptions addressing required criteria are provided for every performance site.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of Procedures (Vertebrate Animals Section)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise description of the proposed procedures to be used that involve live vertebrate animals in the work outlined in the Research Strategy section. Identify the species, strains, ages, sex, and total number of animals by species to be used in the proposed work. If dogs or cats are proposed, provide the source of the animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VAS typically 1–2 pages; must include sufficient detail to allow evaluation (a coherent, albeit brief, description). Examples of procedures to describe: behavioral tests, blood collection, surgical procedures, administration of substances, tumor induction, post-irradiation procedures. Required animal descriptors: species, strains, ages, sex, total number by species; source if dogs or cats. Do not attempt to circumvent page limits by moving substantive material elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for species selection and alternatives (Justifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide justification that the species are appropriate for the proposed research. Explain why the research goals cannot be accomplished using an alternative model (e.g., computational, human, invertebrate, in vitro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must indicate why goals cannot be accomplished using mathematical models, computer simulation, or in vitro systems. Provide rationale for choice of species (advantages and why alternatives are not appropriate). Discuss why less highly evolved or simpler animal models are not appropriate; thoroughly justify use of non-human primates, dogs, or cats. Note: justification for number/sex/ages and other biological variables should be described in the Research Strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for number, sex, ages, and biological variables
rubrics_metrics.description: The justification for the number of animals, sex, ages, and other biological variables should be described in the Research Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sample size rationale and biological-variable choices (power, variability, sex-as-biological-variable considerations). Reviewers will expect these quantitative/experimental- design justifications in the Research Strategy rather than solely in VAS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of pain and distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the interventions including analgesia, anesthesia, sedation, palliative care, and humane endpoints to minimize discomfort, distress, pain, and injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify procedures or circumstances that may result in more than momentary discomfort and describe: interventions to alleviate discomfort/distress/pain; name or class of pharmacological agents if used (e.g., tranquilizers, analgesics, anesthetics, antibiotics) and describe their use; any non-pharmaceutical means to avoid discomfort (including palliative care); manner, circumstances, and duration of post-surgical provisions and care; special housing following surgery/manipulations if necessary; procedures that might lead to severe discomfort/distress/pain/injury; indicators for humane endpoints and euthanasia (e.g., severe infection, respiratory distress, failure to eat, tumor size). Emphasize provisions for survival surgeries and justification for multiple surgeries and measures to avoid complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific agents and post-operative care
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify (by name or class) any tranquilizers, analgesics, anesthetics, and other treatments (e.g., antibiotics) and describe their use. Describe plans for post-surgical care, if survival surgeries are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about drug names/doses/administration schedules or, at minimum, class and intended use. Describe monitoring, duration of analgesic regimen, post-op housing and monitoring, and criteria for escalation or euthanasia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane endpoints and indicators for euthanasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe indicators for humane experimental endpoints and euthanasia (e.g., severe infection, respiratory distress, failure to eat, tumor size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify objective criteria and monitoring schedules that will trigger humane endpoints. If death is not an endpoint, state this and describe alternatives and monitoring to avoid severe outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of euthanasia and AVMA consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a justification for methods of euthanasia that are not consistent with the American Veterinary Medical Association (AVMA) Guidelines for the Euthanasia of Animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If answer is 'No' to 'Is method consistent with AVMA guidelines?', describe the method and provide a scientific justification in the text field provided (Cover Page Supplement / PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form). NIH requires euthanasia to be conducted according to AVMA Guidelines unless scientifically justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: VAS length, page-limit and FOIA disclosure considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, all of the required elements for the VAS can be addressed within 1-2 pages. The VAS must not be used to circumvent page limits. Applicants should be aware that NIH may release information contained in funded applications pursuant to a Freedom of Information Act request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep VAS concise and self-contained. Do not move other research-critical information into VAS to bypass Research Strategy page limits. Be mindful that text in funded applications can be released via FOIA, so confidential details should be considered accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility to address all criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the criteria must be addressed in NIH applications. Failure to adequately address the criteria may negatively affect the application’s impact score. The VAS must not be used to circumvent page limits and is only to include a description of the proposed use of live animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every checklist item is explicitly addressed in the application. Omissions can lead to negative reviewer assessment and lower impact scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation standard (ACCEPTABLE vs UNACCEPTABLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of scientific review groups (SRGs) must evaluate the criteria to determine if plans for the use of vertebrate animals are appropriate relative to the scientific work proposed. All of the items must be evaluated by reviewers as appropriate for an application to be rated as ACCEPTABLE. An application will be rated UNACCEPTABLE if all required items are not addressed adequately or found inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess each required item and judge whether plans are appropriate. Applications with inadequately addressed or inappropriate vertebrate-animal plans receive an UNACCEPTABLE rating; NIH program staff may then request additional information or clarification if recommending funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH administrative, program and grants management verification responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Review staff performs an administrative review checking that all criteria are addressed; program staff obtains additional information or clarification and works with the applicant to resolve animal welfare concerns for any application found to be UNACCEPTABLE; Grants Management staff verifies that the institutional Animal Welfare Assurance number is provided and obtains verification of IACUC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are subject to administrative checks beyond peer review. Applicants should ensure institutional assurances and IACUC approvals are in order and be prepared to supply clarifications if program staff requests them to resolve welfare concerns prior to funding.
